split.label: Read NoC Introduction I.1–I.3: the random walker, and why a uniform distribution looks wrong. (Local PDF pp.1–26.)
Then the Introduction I.4–I.6: non-uniform & Gaussian distributions, then Perlin noise.
Read NoC Ch.1 1.1–1.3: what a vector is, adding and subtracting them.
Then NoC Ch.1 1.4–1.6: scaling, magnitude, and normalization.
Read NoC Ch.2 2.1–2.3: Newton’s laws, and a = F/m as code.
Then NoC Ch.2 2.4–2.5: force accumulation, and what mass changes.
Read NoC Ch.2 2.6: modeling gravity as weight (m·g) — not as attraction.
Then NoC Ch.2 2.7–2.8: friction, and air/fluid resistance.
Read NoC Ch.3 3.1–3.3: angles, angular motion, and trig on screen.
Then NoC Ch.3 3.4–3.5: polar ↔ Cartesian, the conversion the whole burst depends on.
Read NoC Ch.3 3.6–3.8: amplitude, period, and waves.
Then NoC Ch.3 3.9–3.10: the pendulum, and spring forces (Hooke’s law F = −k·x).
Read NoC Ch.4 4.1–4.3: a Particle (pos/vel/acc/lifespan), and an array of them.
Then NoC Ch.4 4.4–4.5: the ParticleSystem class, and a system of systems.
Read The Book of Shaders Ch.1: what a fragment shader is — one program, run per pixel.
Then BoS Ch.2: GLSL, Hello World, uniforms and gl_FragCoord.
Read BoS Ch.3.1: step, smoothstep, and sin/cos shaping functions.
Then BoS Ch.3.2: mix, gradients, and HSB colour.
Read BoS Ch.4.1–4.4: random on the GPU, and controlling chaos.
Then BoS Ch.4.5–4.8: 2D value & gradient noise, and using noise.
Read BoS Ch.5 up to kernel convolution: textures and blend modes.
Then the rest of BoS Ch.5: kernel convolution and the Gaussian blur.
